terms.gloss: chamber pot, usable for a child’s potty
a pot for liquids; a chamber pot
evidence: Plaut. Most. 386: nisi mihi matulam datis
Paul. ex Fest. p. 125: matula vās ūrīnae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Ante- and post-classical (Lewis & Short); matella is its diminutive. Also a term of abuse, “you pot”: numquam ego tē tam esse matulam crēdidī (Plaut. Pers. 533).

phrases.english: Do you want to sit on the potty?

phrases.latin: Jam hercle ego vōs prō matulā habēbō, nisi mihi matulam datis.
phrases.english: By Hercules, I’ll use you for a chamber pot in a moment if you don’t give me one.

sources: Lewis & Short: matella · Lewis & Short: matula
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 289, 363.
